chunks: We were informed by Ali ibn Ahmad, from Ubaydillah ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn Musa, who said: Ahmad ibn Abu Ahmad, known as Abu Ja'far al-Warraq, informed me, from Isma'il ibn Ayyash, from Muhajir ibn Hakim, from al-Mughira ibn Sa'id, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) that he said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said:

"When the two spears (armies) clash in Sham, it will not conclude except with a sign of Allah." It was asked: "What is it, O Commander of the Faithful?" He said: "An earthquake will occur in Sham, in which more than one hundred thousand people will perish. Allah will make it a mercy for the believers and a torment for the disbelievers. When that happens, look for the riders of the gray horses with the cropped tails and the yellow banners, coming from the West until they settle in Sham. This will be at the time of the Great Panic and the Red Death. When that occurs, look for the sinking of a village of Damascus called Harasta. When that happens, the Son of the Liver-Eater will emerge from the dry valley until he stands on the pulpit of Damascus. When that happens, await the emergence of al-Mahdi."

key_terms.ابْنُ آكِلَةِ الْأَكْبَادِ: Son of the Liver-Eater (title for Sufyani)
key_terms.الرِّمَاحَانِ: The two spears (referring to two armies)

ai.seo_question: What are the major signs in Sham before the appearance of Imam al-Mahdi according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (as) links the Sufyani’s rise to the 'Major Signs' (Al-Ayat al-Kubra), specifically identifying the 'earthquake in Sham' as a divine mercy for believers and punishment for disbelievers, a concept rooted in Shia eschatological tradition. The text highlights the Sufyani’s emergence from the 'Valley of Dryness' to Damascus, serving as the immediate precursor to the Mahdi’s appearance, thereby anchoring the political turmoil of the end times within a framework of divine justice and preparation for the global reign of Islam.
